title: Motor effect F = BIL
examples: How do I find the direction of the force on a wire?
What is the relationship between current and motor force?
Can you show me how a simple motor works?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the motor effect in physics. This shows how electricity creates movement. We will look at the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

First we look at Fleming's left-hand rule. This rule helps us find the direction of the force. Remember your thumb shows the force direction. Your forefinger shows the magnetic field direction. Your middle finger shows the current direction.

Next we explore the basic DC motor. A simple motor uses magnets and electricity to make things spin. The current flowing through the coil creates a turning force. This force causes the motor to rotate continuously.

draw.text: DC Motor: Uses magnetism and current

explain.say: The force on the wire is proportional to the current and the field strength. If you increase the current, the force acting on the wire increases. This makes the motor spin faster.

In a real motor, the force acts on both sides of the coil. This balanced force creates a continuous turning effect. The commutator helps reverse the current direction. This allows for continuous rotation.

In everyday life, electric motors are everywhere around us. Think about a toy car powered by batteries. The motor uses the motor effect to move the wheels. The force generated turns the axle, making the car go.

faq.q: What is the motor effect exactly?
faq.a: The motor effect is the production of continuous rotational force when an electric current passes through a coil placed in a magnetic field. It is the principle behind electric motors.
asks: How does electricity make things turn?
What causes a motor to spin?

faq.q: How do I use Fleming's left-hand rule?
faq.a: You point your forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, your middle finger shows the direction of the current, and your thumb points in the direction of the force. This determines the force direction.
asks: What do the fingers show for force?
Which finger is for the magnetic field?

faq.q: Does the force depend on the strength of the magnets?
faq.a: Yes, the force is directly proportional to the strength of the magnetic field. Stronger magnets create a stronger field, leading to a greater force.
asks: What if the field is weak?

faq.q: Why does the motor keep spinning?
faq.a: The motor uses a commutator to periodically reverse the direction of the current in the coil. This ensures that the force continues to push in the same rotational direction.

faq.q: Is the force only on the wires?
faq.a: The force acts on the sides of the conductor that are perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field lines. This force creates the torque needed for rotation.
asks: Does the force act on the whole coil?

facts: The motor effect demonstrates that electricity can produce mechanical work.
Fleming's left-hand rule is used to determine the direction of the force.
The force (F) is directly proportional to the current (I), the length (L), and the magnetic field strength (B).
A commutator is essential in a DC motor to maintain continuous rotation.

quiz.say: If the current through the coil is doubled, what happens to the force, keeping all else constant?

options.show: The force will stay the same.
options.say: The force will stay the same.

quiz.why: The formula shows that force is directly proportional to current, so doubling the current doubles the force.

wrong.0: This suggests an inverse relationship, which is incorrect for this effect.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes the relationship is quadratic, when it is linear.
wrong.3: This ignores the direct relationship between current and force.

quiz.say: Which part of the motor reverses the current to keep it spinning?
quiz.why: The commutator is specifically designed to reverse the current flow periodically, maintaining the turning force.

wrong.0: The magnets provide the field, but the commutator manages the current direction.
wrong.1: The coil carries the current; it is not the part responsible for reversing the flow.
wrong.3: The switch only opens or closes the circuit, it does not reverse the current.

quiz.say: According to Fleming's rule, if the field is North to South, and the current is up, what is the force direction?

options.show: The force is to the left.
options.say: The force is to the left.

options.show: The force is to the right.
options.say: The force is to the right.

quiz.why: Following the rule: Field (B) is right, Current (I) is up, so the Force (F) must be to the left.

wrong.1: This ignores the direction of the magnetic field provided.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes the force opposes the current direction.
wrong.3: This would happen if the current was pointing in the opposite direction.
